Activation-patching research offers useful methods, but transfer to BERT4Rec remains a hypothesis. [Zhang & Nanda, ICLR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) show that corruption choices and measurement metrics can substantially change localization results; [Heimersheim & Nanda, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255) explain complementary clean-to-corrupted and corrupted-to-clean interventions. [MIB, ICML 2025](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/mueller25a.html) evaluates circuit faithfulness across sizes and against random controls. Proposed application: patch attention outputs, feed-forward outputs, and residual states between matched histories; measure target-versus-negative score margins alongside ranking changes. Include identical-input patches, random donor patches, equally sized random component sets, and restoration checks. Layer ablation alone establishes sensitivity to intervention, not a uniquely identified mechanism.

Sequential-recommendation evidence motivates separating position and popularity effects: [Learning Positional Attention, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02793) finds learned positional embeddings often encode token distance; [Lin et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12008) connect popularity amplification to dominant score-matrix spectral components. For the single trained BERT4Rec, proposed controls are item replacement matched on training frequency, history permutation preserving the item multiset, and position-embedding interventions preserving content. Keep left padding and appended-mask readout fixed; patch aligned nonpadding positions. Embedding-norm/frequency correlations are descriptive evidence, requiring controlled interventions before claiming shortcuts. Check activation norms and unchanged unpatched paths to detect intervention artifacts. Report training-prefix mechanism measurements separately from held-out macro validation HR@10: faithful recovery of model behavior does not establish recommendation usefulness.
